content: Before taking rilpivirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. If you are pregnant, notify your doctor before using this medication, as treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Be aware that this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of rilpivirine from your body, potentially impacting its effectiveness. Examples include dexamethasone, macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin), and rifamycins (such as rifampin and rifapentine). In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (such as viral load, T-cell counts, and liver function) should be conducted. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it with a meal as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Rilpivirine is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications (such as new infections or cancer) and improves your quality of life. It is typically prescribed to individuals who have not previously taken HIV medications. Rilpivirine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) and is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use an effective barrier method (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items (such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors) that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting rilpivirine and each time you get a refill. Take this medication by mouth with a meal as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage may depend on other medications you are taking. Medications that reduce or block stomach acid (such as proton pump inhibitors [PPIs], H2 blockers, or antacids) may decrease the absorption of rilpivirine, reducing its effectiveness. Do not take PPIs (such as omeprazole or lansoprazole) while using this medication. If you take antacids, take them at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take less of this drug than prescribed or stop taking it (or other HIV medicines) even for a short time unless directed to do so by your doctor. Do not increase your dose or take this medication more often than prescribed. For the best effect, take this medication at evenly spaced times. Common side effects include headache or difficulty sleeping. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or many months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication (e.g., increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas, decreased fat in the arms and legs). The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Rilpivirine can commonly cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
